## Journey

- Age 14, Dominican Republic: taught himself to code by building a small platformer game. Self-taught through constant practice. The game led to a referral for his first job.
- 2019, Softone (Santo Domingo): first professional role, building a desktop ERP the business relied on every day.
- 2020, ITelle (Santo Domingo): first team lead role across varied client projects, including publishing mobile apps to the app stores and owning deployments.
- 2022, remote: Drimo, then ListoApp (Chile), building mobile apps and multi-tenant platforms.
- 2024, Georgia, United States: moved to the US and works remotely on hotel connectivity at PriceTravel Holding.
- Now: looking for a team to connect with, where he can bring AI-powered ways of building software and ship products that solve concrete problems, end to end. Off the clock he vibe-codes games, explores generative AI, runs, and goes to the gym. Motto: never stop learning.

## Selected Work

### Sócrates: exam prep in minutes, not hours

Problem: Dominican teachers spent 40–90 minutes turning official MINERD curriculum into a usable exam.
Result: Sócrates generates an editable, curriculum-grounded DOCX exam in 10–15 minutes (about 75% less prep time).
Stack: Document AI, OCR, structured extraction, DOCX generation.
Project URL: https://socrates.xavely.com

### Hotel quotes that stay in sync with live inventory

Problem: Quoting depended on many hotel providers with different behaviors and latency.
Result: Carlos built and hardened the provider connections and cached exchange rates and promotions. The quoting engine gets fresh rates and availability while hitting the database less.
Providers: SiteMinder (SiteConnect), TravelClick, Omnibees, Gin RateFox, and TravelGate HotelX (built); Hotelbeds, DerbySoft, SynXis, and Expedia Rapid API (optimized).
Stack: AWS DAX, background workers, hotel provider APIs.
Project URL: https://pricetravel.com

### One platform for insurers, providers, and agents

Problem: Two growing SaaS products needed to serve several user roles on shared infrastructure.
Result: Carlos built the backends behind Sektor.app and Centuria.app, with event-driven notifications that keep every party in the loop as work moves forward.
Stack: TypeScript, NestJS, GraphQL, MongoDB, AWS SNS/EventBridge.
Project URL: https://sektor.app/

### Live results from 128 sources, in real time

Problem: A live-data product needed fast-changing results from 128 roulette tables delivered to users instantly and without duplicates.
Result: Carlos built a concurrent collection pipeline and a real-time API that streams one clean event per change.
Stack: Go, WebSockets, Chrome-based scraping.
Project URL: https://roulettesview.com

## Experience and Improvements

- PriceTravel Holding — Backend Developer, Hotel Connectivity & Quoting (Jun 2024 – Present, remote from the US). Built 5 new hotel provider integrations and hardened 4 existing ones; cached exchange rates and promotions in DAX so quotes stopped repeating database queries; improved currency conversion accuracy with the quoting team.
- ListoApp (Chile) — Backend Developer, SaaS Platforms & Cloud (Feb 2024 – 2026, remote). Cut AWS Lambda cold-start time by 50% with pre-deployment bundling; event-driven notifications with SNS and EventBridge; real-time API streaming results from 128 sources; CI/CD with GitHub Actions.
- Drimo — Software Developer (Jul 2022 – Jun 2023, remote). Migrated the website and blog to Next.js for faster loads and better SEO; made serverless APIs on AWS more reliable and cheaper to run.
- ITelle — Team Lead (2020 – 2022, Santo Domingo). Led the team across varied client projects; published mobile apps to the app stores; owned deployments and production operation.
- Softone — Software Developer (2019 – 2020, Santo Domingo). First professional role, building a desktop ERP.

The full skills inventory is on the CV.
